- `minds-admin archives create` now archives workspaces running under gVisor (`runsc`), which is every gen-2 slice. It refused them with "the workspace's container layer path is not absolute: ''" because it read the container's writable layer off the container pid's own mount table, and a runsc container's pid is the sandbox process, whose root is a tmpfs. The command now also reads the VM's mount table, where dockerd mounts the container's rootfs overlay at `<data-root>/rootfs/overlayfs/<full container id>`. runc containers are unchanged. Found while retiring a `minds-v0.6.2` staging workspace on 2026-09-19.

- `minds-admin cutover migrate` now starts the template's `minds-autostart.service` on the migrated VM after running the version's autostart installer. The `minds-v0.3.11` template's installer only enables that unit for the next boot (every later tag starts it itself), and the migrate runs the installer on an already-booted VM, so a 0.3.11 workspace came back with its container up but no services agent, no supervisord, and no UI, and failed the health probe with the row parked. Found on the first `minds-v0.3.11` production migration on 2026-09-20.

- `minds-admin cutover migrate`'s health probe now requires only the supervisord programs the workspace's release template ships (its `system/supervisord.conf` and drop-ins, read from the tag it already clones). A program the owner added to their workspace's supervisord that is not running no longer fails the probe and parks the row; it is reported in the workspace's outcome (`owner-added program not running: <name> <STATE>`) and the log, since it is the owner's to fix. Found on 2026-09-20 when a production workspace's own program died under gVisor (`ionice: ioprio_set failed: Operation not permitted`) while every template service, the UI and latchkey were healthy. The preflight, which knows no version yet, still counts every program.

- `minds-admin archives create` no longer fails the whole archive on a file whose mtime is later than 2107. The zip streamer clamped timestamps before 1980 (the DOS date field's floor) but not after its ceiling, so one pytest fixture file with a synthetic far-future mtime left under a workspace's `/tmp` made the stdlib overflow the date field (`struct.error: ushort format requires 0 <= number <= 65535`) and the run exit 1 after the workspace had been admin-started. Such timestamps are now clamped to the ceiling, like the floor. Found on 2026-09-20 while archiving two production workspaces for their owner.

- `minds-admin cutover migrate --shrink-oversized-disks` transplants a gen-1 data disk larger than the default gen-2 size into a default-size disk (44 GiB at 8 units) and restamps the row's `disk_gb`, when the disk's used bytes fit beside the gen-2 base and system reserve; a disk that would not fit is refused at the harvest with the workspace still running, and a rollback stamps the original `disk_gb` back. Without the flag nothing changes. Needed for the six workspaces on the 8 TB vin box, whose 216 GiB gen-1 disks (232 GiB rows) hold 1.5 to 5 GB each and would otherwise each charge 242 GiB of a 14-slot target's 808 GiB budget.

- `minds-admin cutover migrate` now repairs a replayed workspace whose `mngr` tool environment no longer matches its vendored mngr: when the autostart unit fails to start after the replay, the migrate rebuilds the tool inside the container from the workspace's own `system/vendor/mngr` and the plugins `system/config/mngr_plugins.toml` assigns it (the template's own `install_mngr.py` procedure, pinned to the tool home a login shell resolves) and retries the start once. A workspace that self-updated after its bake, or rolled an update back, ships a release image whose tool registers a plugin the volume's tree cannot import (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'imbue.mngr_autocompact.plugin'`, or a missing `watchdog`), so `mngr start` died at import and the row stayed parked until an operator ran the reinstall by hand; that happened on three production migrations before this, the third on 2026-09-21, where a re-run could not resume because each replay recreates the container and discards the hand fix.

- `minds-admin cutover migrate` now gives a replayed latchkey gateway the curl its harvested run script names. The run script is written by the owner's desktop, and a desktop build that installs the curl shim under another name than the migrate's own latchkey provisioning (`latchkey-curl-router` against this build's `latchkey-curl-dispatch`) left the gateway exiting at once with "'/usr/local/bin/latchkey-curl-router' is not available" and the row parked after the health probe. The replay now reads the `LATCHKEY_CURL` path off the harvested script and, when it is absent on the new VM, symlinks it onto the installed shim; the desktop's next provisioning pass replaces the link with its own binary. Found on 2026-09-21 on a production workspace whose owner runs a desktop from an unmerged branch.
